props.gloss_en: one does not fulfil his obligation on the first festival day with another's lulav
'and you shall take' -- that the taking be in the hand of each and every one
the source: 'for yourselves' (lachem, Lev 23:40)
the criterion: 'for yourselves' -- from your own; the first-day taking must be of one's own
the bridge: to exclude the borrowed -- a borrowed lulav is not 'yours'
and to exclude the stolen
unless the other gave it to him as a gift
the maaseh: RG, R' Yehoshua, R' Elazar ben Azarya and R' Akiva on a ship, only RG having a lulav; each took it, fulfilled with it, and gave it to the next as a gift
only Rabban Gamliel had a lulav, which he bought for a thousand zuz
R' Akiva took it, fulfilled with it, and returned it to Rabban Gamliel
a gift on condition of return is called a gift
Rava: 'here is this etrog on condition that you return it to me' -- he took it and fulfilled with it: if he returned it, he fulfilled
Rava: if he did not return it, he did not fulfil
to tell you how beloved the mitzvot were to them
Mar bar Ameimar: my father would pray with it [the lulav in hand]
one may not hold tefillin in his hand or a Torah scroll in his lap and pray, nor urinate with them, nor sleep with them, neither fixed nor casual sleep
Shmuel: a knife, a bowl, a loaf and coins are like them
R' Elazar bar Tzadok: the custom of the people of Jerusalem -- the lulav in hand leaving home, going to synagogue, reciting Shema and praying, visiting the sick and comforting mourners
reading the Torah and lifting his hands [in the priestly blessing] he lays it on the ground; entering the beit midrash he sends his lulav with his son, his slave or his agent
to tell you how zealous they were in mitzvot

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: לא יאחז אדם תפילין בידו וספר תורה בחיקו ויתפלל... ואמר שמואל: סכין וקערה ככר ומעות הרי אלו כיוצא בהן -- holding objects while praying is forbidden, so how could Ameimar pray holding the lulav?
